changes.reason: The reviewer diagnosed this finding as a tool defect rather than an over-long sentence, and demonstrated it by feeding the masked text straight to sentence-splitter: masking a markdown link destination together with its closing `]` left the opening `[` unpaired, so the splitter treated the remainder of the block as bracketed and merged several sentences into one 55-word span. The defect was corrected in linkDestinationPass (the mask now keeps brackets balanced) and the finding no longer occurs, so expectedDiagnostics is empty. The prose was left unchanged.
semanticInvariants: the four-sentence description of how an audit event is generated, pre-processed, and persisted must remain unchanged
the markdown link to the kube-apiserver reference page must remain unchanged

changes.reason: Unambiguous contraction in 'The policy determines what's recorded' -- clearly 'what is recorded' (present tense), not 'what has recorded' which would be ungrammatical here. Expanding it changes nothing about meaning.
semanticInvariants: the claim that policy determines what is recorded, and backends persist the records, must be preserved

notes: The single sentence-length-descriptive finding is disputed as an empirically-verified tool artifact: masking the markdown link destination breaks the sentence-splitter for the remainder of the paragraph, merging four short, correct sentences into one falsely 'overlong' one. The only genuine, safe defect (an unambiguous contraction) is accepted. Passage p1 records a segmentation defect found through this corpus and since fixed in the analyser; it is retained as the audit trail for that discovery.
